requirements.statement: Every transmit timestamp MUST carry the identifier the socket announced for its frame, also after a send the kernel refused (Linux 6.13 and later).

acceptance.given: 1 000 frames sent in single and batched sends with software transmit timestamps on veth
acceptance.then: their identifiers are exactly the announced ones

acceptance.given: a send refused by an etf qdisc (past launch time)
acceptance.then: their timestamps carry the identifiers announced for them

tasks.text: [US1] [SR-001] src/sys/linux.rs: socket flags (`TX_SOFTWARE|SOFTWARE|OPT_ID|OPT_TSONLY`, plus `TX_HARDWARE|RAW_HARDWARE` when the NIC stamps); `send`, `send_at`, `send_batch` go through `sendmsg`/`sendmmsg` with an `SCM_TS_OPT_ID` cmsg (and `SCM_TXTIME` for `send_at`) when stamping; id mode Explicit→Implicit on the kernel's `EINVAL` with one retry; `next_tx_id` wraps and advances per accepted frame

[US1] [SR-001] tests/veth.rs: 1 000 frames (single and batched, both paths) → timestamps with exactly the announced ids, `Software`, not before the send; after an `etf`-refused send, the next 10 ids match (SR-001 scenario 2; with `RAWETHER_REQUIRE_ETF` in CI); `tx_timestamp(50 ms)` with nothing waiting returns `None` after ≥ 45 ms, and at once when non-blocking (US1 scenario 4); `next_tx_id` wraps (unit test)

requirements.statement: Requesting hardware transmit timestamps MUST NOT change a NIC whose configuration could not be read, MUST raise tx_type only from OFF to ON, and MUST leave every other tx_type and the receive filter rule of 0.1.0 unchanged.

acceptance.given: every tx_type 0..=3, rx_filter 0..=15, and receive/transmit requests
acceptance.then: a write raises tx_type only from OFF to ON, rx_filter only from NONE to ALL, and changes nothing else

tasks.text: [SR-002] src/hwtstamp.rs: `decide(current, want_rx, want_tx)`; a write only raises rx_filter NONE→ALL (want_rx) and tx_type OFF→ON (want_tx); `Effective { rx, tx }` from the final configuration; exhaustive test over flags × tx_type 0..=3 × rx_filter 0..=15 × the four request combinations

[US3] [SR-002] src/sys/linux.rs: `hardware_timestamps` uses the new `decide` for receive and transmit together, one read and at most one write; `tx_timestamping()` reports the effective mode; veth: Hardware requested → Software reported

requirements.statement: Unread transmit timestamps MUST NOT make a receive spin, and rawether MUST keep at most a fixed number of them, counting the ones it drops.

acceptance.given: a socket with transmit timestamps and 2 000 frames sent without reading their timestamps
acceptance.then: it returns after about 200 ms using little CPU, 1 024 timestamps can be read, and the lost count is the rest
acceptance.when: recv waits 200 ms with nothing to receive

tasks.text: [US1] [SR-003] src/sys/linux.rs: bounded queue (1 024, preallocated) with `timestamps_lost`; `tx_timestamp(timeout)` waits on POLLERR only (events 0), surfaces socket errors; recv's error path fills the same queue

[US4] [SR-003] [SR-004] tests/veth.rs: 2 000 unread stamps → `recv(200 ms)` returns after ~200 ms, 1 024 readable, `timestamps_lost` = 976; `etf` + stamping: refused launch time counted `invalid` = 1 and every sent frame's stamp read, in both reading orders

requirements.statement: Reading transmit timestamps MUST NOT discard launch-time reports, and reading launch-time reports MUST NOT discard timestamps.

acceptance.given: a socket with launch times and transmit timestamps through etf, one refused launch time and frames that left
acceptance.then: invalid = 1 and every sent frame's timestamp is there
acceptance.when: tx_errors and the timestamps are read in either order
